:::{#hero-heading}

Thanks for stopping by!

I’m Richard Liu, a Ph.D. trainee at NYU Grossman School of Medicine, supervised by [Dr. Ivan Diaz](https://idiaz.xyz/). I’m fortunate to collaborate with researchers including [Dr. Wenbo Wu](https://www.wenbowu.me/), [Dr. Kara Rudolph](https://kararudolph.github.io/), [Dr. Michele Santacatterina](https://michelesantacatterina.github.io/), and [Dr. Alex Luedtke](https://alexluedtke.com/). I also work as a research assistant with [Dr. David M. Charytan](https://nyulangone.org/doctors/1649261264/david-m-charytan) and [Dr. Jiyuan Hu](https://med.nyu.edu/faculty/jiyuan-hu), among others.

I’m, in general, interested in developing and applying modern statistical and machine learning methods to questions in public health and medicine. My research focuses on causal machine learning, semiparametric theory, mediation analysis, and causal inference with time-varying treatments and outcomes. I’ve also worked on projects involving transportability, causal fairness, and applications of large language models (LLMs) to causal inference.

Outside of research, I am also interested in a lot of activities, including cooking, exercising, including fitness training and archery, and playing card and video games.

Please feel free to reach out if you’re interested in collaborating!

## Education

- PhD, NYU Grossman School of Medicine, Expected 2027

## Experience

- Ph.D. Statistics Intern, Eli Lilly and Company, 05/2026-08/2026

## Service

- Student committee member, [Society of Causal Inference (SCI)](https://sci-info.org/), Current
- Teaching Assistant of Data analysis and biostatistics in R (2025, 2026 Fall), Regression Analysis (2026 Spring) and Statistical Inference (2026 Spring) in NYU Grossman School of Medicine
